notes: Myer Home (myer.com.au), Home department only. Access: tier-1 direct HTTP (curl_cffi impersonate chrome124) worked for every page, no WAF/block encountered, consistent with prior Home-Decor pass notes/188.md. robots.txt checked first: no Claude-specific disallow; general disallows (women/men/beauty/kidsbaby/electrical/gifts/offers/, /promo/, /just-landed-709561--1/, facets/sort/search/account/login) do not cover the URL paths used here (/c/new-in/... and /c/home/...), so none were fetched. Platform is the same Next.js + Fredhopper (Attraqt) merchandising engine documented in notes/188.md: every category page's __NEXT_DATA__ react-query cache holds an exact 'productTotalCount' integer, trusted per the prior pass's 6-category exhaustion verification on this same platform; spot-checked stability here by refetching two of the new categoryIds (home-bestsellers, new-in-home shortcut) and total stayed identical across repeat fetches. Discovery: crawled the homepage's full embedded global nav-tree JSON (categoryId/seoToken/childCategories) for 'bestsell', 'best-sell', 'top-sell', 'popular', 'trending', 'customer favourite' - both site-wide English and the AU-English 'favourite' spelling. Found two genuinely distinct Home-scoped Bestsellers-type PLPs (different categoryIds, different product counts, so kept as separate rows per brief 3): (1) 'Home Best Sellers' (categoryId 1732589) nested under the site's 'New In' mega-menu > 'Best Sellers' branch (parallel Women/Men/Kids/Toys/Beauty/Travel&Tech/Home Best Sellers siblings) - a plain leaf listing, no further children. (2) 'Now Trending' / on-page title 'Homewares Inspiration | Now Trending' (categoryId 785588), reached from the main Home department dropdown - opened and confirmed it is a genuine Fredhopper-backed PLP (real productTotalCount, real brand facets e.g. Baccarat/Breville/Essteele/KitchenAid/Krosno, real product names e.g. 'Sandy Cape Washed Belgian Linen Quilt Cover Set'), not an editorial/lookbook page, and its own on-page label 'Now Trending' maps directly to the brief's allowed target term 'Trending Products'. Its one child, 'Spring Home Shop' (seasonal_shop), is a seasonal campaign mini-collection, not a bestseller/trending listing - excluded from this project (belongs to the separate Seasonal extraction, not double-counted here). Also checked and confirmed NOT a Home Bestsellers candidate: 'Home Mid Season Sale' (categoryId 1064077) is a generic temporary percent-off promo, not a popularity/bestseller concept - out of scope for this brief. No PDP-only 'Bestseller' badges were treated as PLPs. Sitemap/footer nav gave no additional Home-scoped bestseller/trending candidates beyond these two.
